paper.title: OMCDE: Opposition-based Multi-Stage Matrix-Based Competitive Differential Evolution
paper.summary: Differential Evolution has proven to be an effective algorithm for continuous global optimization, but it's modern high-performing variants often introduce additional complexity and computational cost. We propose OMCDE, a matrix-based competitive Differential Evolution algorithm that aims to improve optimization performance while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed approach integrates competition-driven search dynamics, adaptive behavior between optimization stages, and opposition-based initialization within a parallelizable framework. Empirical results on widely used CEC 2017 functions show that OMCDE achieves strong performance compared to several state-of-the-art DE algorithms, while remaining efficient and scalable. These findings indicate that OMCDE is a promising alternative for solving complex numerical optimization problems.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the trade-off between optimization performance and computational efficiency in modern high-performing variants of Differential Evolution for continuous global optimization.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Computational efficiency and algorithmic complexity in numerical optimization solvers.
analysis.executive_summary: This work proposes OMCDE, a matrix-based competitive Differential Evolution algorithm that integrates opposition-based initialization and adaptive stage behavior to enhance search dynamics. By maintaining a parallelizable framework, it aims to deliver state-of-the-art performance on CEC 2017 benchmarks without the significant computational overhead associated with other advanced DE variants.
